title: Near-linear output-sensitive Subset Sum
formal: Do there exist a uniform bounded-error randomized word-RAM algorithm and constants \(C>0\), \(b\ge0\) that, given \(n\ge1\) positive integers \(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}\le t\) and an integer \(t\ge1\), output exactly the distinct values in \(S(X,t)=\{\sum_{i\in I}x_{i}:I\subseteq[n]\}\cap\{0,\ldots,t\}\) in at most \(C(n+|S(X,t)|)(\log(n+t+2))^{b}\) operations?
definitions: The input is an explicitly listed multiset; repeated values are allowed and each index can be selected at most once. The empty subset contributes zero. Output every attainable value once, in any order, with no requirement to list subsets or witnesses. Inputs exceeding the threshold can be discarded when represented in the same word model. Use a uniform word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_{2}(n+t+2)\rceil\), for a fixed positive integer \(d\) chosen with the algorithm and large enough for its addresses and input values. Unit-cost instructions are word reads/writes, copying, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), and integer quotient and remainder with nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Multiword computation is charged by its component instructions. The fixed finite program receives no advice or precomputed tables; all initialization, preprocessing and output writes count. Randomness consists of independent uniform random words, each generated at unit cost. On every input, the whole output must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\). The time bound holds for every random execution, including unsuccessful ones. The word-size constant and all time constants are independent of both \(n\) and \(t\). The target permits polylogarithmic dependence on the numerical threshold, but no linear scan of its universe unless covered by the stated output bound.

context_blocks.text: Subset Sum may have very few attainable values below the threshold even when the threshold is huge. Output-sensitive complexity measures the set that must actually be produced, together with reading the input.
Bringmann and Nakos explicitly ask for near-linear time in the number of attainable sums. Their algorithm gives a four-thirds power dependence on the output size.

Chan derandomizes pseudopolynomial Subset Sum in 2026 and also derandomizes the \(\widetilde O(|S|^{4/3})\) and \(\widetilde O(|S|\sqrt n)\) output-sensitive bounds. Those results do not attain the stated near-linear output-sensitive endpoint.

why: This asks whether a fundamental pseudopolynomial problem can be solved at essentially its actual input and output size, avoiding a large unused numerical universe.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

sentences: The input is a multiset of positive integers and a threshold.
The task is to enumerate the distinct attainable subset sums at most that threshold.
The question asks for near-linear time in the explicit input and the actual number of output values.
Known pseudopolynomial algorithms and output-sensitive improvements do not reach this endpoint.
The target avoids spending linear time on a large numerical universe containing few attainable sums.
